reading.body:
AWS generated $717 billion in revenue through 2025 and offers two primary AI product lines: SageMaker for full machine learning lifecycle management and Bedrock for managed foundation model APIs.

The scale of AWS revenue reflects its position as the dominant cloud infrastructure provider globally. Both products sit directly in the compute abstraction layer. SageMaker addresses the full workflow from data ingestion through model deployment and monitoring. Bedrock commodifies access to foundation models themselves, bundling model inference with standard cloud security and orchestration primitives like IAM, VPC, and agent frameworks.

For AI scaling specifically, this matters because neither product appears to address power or physical infrastructure constraints. SageMaker optimizes the software layer above compute. Bedrock abstracts which models run where but does not disclose how AWS has provisioned or will provision the underlying accelerator capacity to serve either product at scale. The data does not show energy efficiency commitments, grid agreements, or datacenter build plans tied to AI demand.

The legal exposure count of 52 records in Washington state indicates regulatory activity, but the data does not identify which concerns apply to AI versus AWS's broader operations, or whether they touch infrastructure, data residency, or other domains material to AI's physical constraints.

profile_text.body:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is a public company headquartered in Seattle, WA, founded in 1994, traded on public markets under the ticker AMZN, and reporting revenues of $716,924,000,000 for the period ending December 31, 2025. The company's website presents Amazon SageMaker as a unified development environment for data, analytics, and machine learning, describing it as bringing together AWS ML and analytics capabilities in a single platform. According to the site, SageMaker Unified Studio supports model development, generative AI, data processing, and SQL analytics, and integrates tools including HyperPod, JumpStart, and MLOps alongside Amazon Q Developer, which the site describes as an AI assistant for software development tasks such as discovering data, building and training models, generating SQL queries, and running data pipeline jobs through natural language.

AWS tracks two AI products on this site: Amazon SageMaker, categorized under Cloud AI Services and Model APIs and noted for full ML lifecycle management, model monitoring, bias detection, and explainability tools, and AWS Bedrock, also in that category, noted as a managed foundation model API service with IAM integration, VPC support, model evaluation tools, and an AgentCore component for agent orchestration. The SageMaker platform, as described on the company's site, supports a lakehouse architecture unifying Amazon S3 data lakes and Amazon Redshift data warehouses, offers Apache Iceberg-compatible query access, and includes governance features such as fine-grained access controls via Amazon SageMaker Catalog, data classification, toxicity detection, guardrails, and responsible AI policies.

The held facts associate AWS with 55 law exposure entries in Washington state, though no specific litigation cases are recorded in the current data. The company holds an SEC filing identity under CIK 0001018724, with its most recent revenue figures drawn from a 10-K filing.
